svg.title: Main loop algorithm — CAD_OpenGL
svg.desc: The application's top-level control flow: sleep until woken by a user input event or a worker-thread completion. Resize is a special exception path that bypasses the normal relevance check and renders immediately. Other user events go through relevance checking, then either update UI-local state or a tool's flow (Prerequisites/Selections, then modifying/calculating/hybrid/settings-change). Worker completions bypass UI's relevance check since Scene already knows the work matters; an Operation/Import completion checks success before committing. Everything converges on one state-changed check before rendering and sleeping again.
svg.text: Main loop — one continuous cycle, sleep to sleep
Sleep until vsync or a wake-up
viewport itself stays fixed size — panels overlay it
bypasses the state-changed check below — already rendering
loop straight back to sleep — does not
touch the relevance check or convergence
UI checks relevance (the only other gate)
global, or tool-specific on its own panel
no UI relevance check — Scene already knows it matters
→ shows progress bar in the meantime
Analysis, not Part), clears pending flag
Every branch above ends at a connector A — converges here, once
Render: read Scene + UI camera + live-preview slot,
bounded time budget per frame — never stutters
no → back to sleep, no redraw
Companion to architecture-diagram.svg (the ownership map). Same abstraction level as the tool
algorithms there — decisions and named steps, not literal code. Rendering's own small features
(z-fighting tie-break, fog) are deliberately left as one line in the Render box — see the ownership
map for their origin/reasoning, not duplicated here.
